claim: TIMBRE PARAMETERS ESTIMATED FROM A SMALL NUMBER OF SAMPLES, WITH LEAVE-ONE-UTTERANCE-OUT ERROR QUANTIFIED. This is NOT voice cloning: no audio was heard, no perceptual judgement was made, and the descriptors are five scalars fitted to a very small corpus.
not_claimed: an absolute formant scale for a single speaker (only the ratio between speakers is identified; see formant_scale_reference)
f3_reason: step 2 measured F3 to be systematically 158-420 Hz too high and could not remove the bias with any LPC order (18/20/22/24) or lag window; a scale factor fitted on a biased axis would fold that bias into the 'speaker' parameter, so F1/F2 only are used everywhere

SSB0502.f0_source: step 2 speakers[<speaker>]['f0_hz'] (mean over that speaker's voiced samples; step 2 stored no per-syllable F0, so no median could be computed independently here)

bandwidth_scale_info.reason: phoneme_params.json['phonemes'][*]['per_speaker'] stores only 'n' and 'formants'; the only bandwidths are pooled over both speakers, so no per-speaker bandwidth ratio can be formed

SSB0502.warp_note: alpha knee of Bark(f/alpha)*alpha fitted jointly with formant_scale; alpha near the middle of a wide flat minimum means the warp carries no information beyond the scale
SSB0502.confidence_rule: high: >= 3 usable phonemes; low: < 3 (insufficient samples: does not represent this speaker)
SSB0502.spectral_tilt_method: LTAS: 720 Hz Hamming frames every 480 samples over the whole utterance, frames >= max(0.10*peak, peak-30dB), power-mean magnitude, 1/3-octave triangular smoothing, least squares of 20log10|X| vs log2(f) over 80-8000 Hz
SSB0502.spectral_tilt_approximation: naive band-limited DFT (no FFT), half-hop frames, 1/3-octave band averaging and a bounded utterance sample -- an approximation of the LTAS, not an exact one
SSB0502.row_note: n_rows > n_phonemes is expected: step 2 repeats one phoneme across many syllables; independent samples are the phoneme count, not the row count

cross_validation.prediction_units: Bark distance between predicted and observed F1/F2
cross_validation.note: model = per-phone measured mean x phone correction x speaker scale fitted without the held-out utterance; baseline = speaker-blind per-phone mean; oracle = same-speaker per-phone mean (ceiling)

f0_holdout.unavailable_reason: no per-syllable F0 anywhere in phoneme_params.json: the 'provenance' rows carry utterance/speaker/pinyin/start/end/formants/bound_confidence/split_confidence and no f0_hz, and 'per_speaker' carries only n + formants. Step 2 kept one pooled f0_hz per phoneme and one per speaker, which cannot be split into held-out utterances, so F0 is reported as a point estimate with a source label and NOT as a validated error.
f0_holdout.consequence: f0_hz in a speaker entry is a point estimate of the speaker's F0 level; its held-out prediction error is unknown from this table

verdict.finding: the speaker-scale model is NOT better than the speaker-blind per-phone mean on this data; the fitted descriptor carries no usable formant information beyond phoneme identity
verdict.oracle_ceiling_note: oracle uses same-speaker repeats of the same phoneme, so it is a ceiling, not an achievable method; the gap between model and oracle is what the scalar descriptors fail to capture
verdict.fraction_of_oracle_gain_note: undefined: the speaker-blind baseline is already at or below the same-speaker oracle, so there is no gain to attribute

shift_vs_spread.interpretation: the descriptors move a prediction by this fraction of the leftover scatter they are supposed to explain
shift_vs_spread.conclusion: the fitted speaker descriptors are far too small, relative to same-phoneme scatter across utterances, to improve a formant prediction. This is why the model does not beat the baseline, and it also means the measured speaker differences are near the noise floor of this corpus

model_shift_from_baseline_bark.description: Bark distance between the model's prediction and the speaker-blind baseline prediction, per scored syllable; this is how much the fitted descriptors actually move a prediction

honest_negative_finding.result: NEGATIVE: the speaker-scale model does not beat the baseline
honest_negative_finding.headline: leave-one-utterance-out, the fit speaker descriptors are worse than simply predicting each phoneme's speaker-blind mean
honest_negative_finding.why: the descriptors move a prediction by only 0.0312 Bark while the leftover same-phoneme scatter they are meant to explain is 0.6531 Bark, i.e. under 5 %. The speaker differences in this corpus are near its noise floor, so a scalar formant scale cannot help on this data
what_follows: the two speakers are NOT shown to be separable in formants: the measured F1/F2 distance is inside the cross-validated error
the speaker tables were still emitted, because they are the honest point estimates the samples were rendered from and collapsing them to 1.0 would hide the measurement
this was reported, not tuned away: no per-phone subset, alpha range, or fold definition was adjusted to flip the verdict
honest_negative_finding.what_would_be_needed: per-syllable audio re-analysis (so F0 and bandwidths are usable per speaker) and more than 3 utterances per phoneme, or a descriptor that models spectral detail rather than F1/F2
